subject: secr bug fixed: model.average() with parameter 'pmix'

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: secr bug fixed: model.average() with parameter 'pmix'
parts:
The parameter 'pmix' in finite mixture models is an odd one. It always uses an mlogit link, which makes for trouble in the coding. Ordinarily I would say it makes no sense to model average pmix estimates, because the value of pmix is entirely dependent on the g0 (lambda0) and sigma values for each latent class. That is my excuse for not ensuring that model.average worked with pmix (it didn't). However, the 'hcov' hybrid mixture model mechanism ties down the class definitions when a substantial proportion of individuals are of known class, and then the classes are no longer 'latent', which makes model.averaging more sensible. This is how I see it anyway - other opinions welcome. (For a null detection model when all individuals are of known class, pmix is simply the observed proportion in each class).

This preamble leads up to the news that I have patched model.average() in secr so that it works with pmix, at least in the 2-class (h2) case. The revised version is available as secr 2.9.6 at www.otago.ac.nz/density/SECRinR.html until a new version of secr appears on CRAN in a few weeks (vagueness is deliberate). I would be glad to hear of any further difficulties with model.average(). Thanks to Fridolin Zimmermann for raising the problem.

Murray
